title: Anatomy of an HTML Element 🔍
description: Tags, content, attributes – understand what makes an HTML element.

slides.title: What Exactly is an Element? 🧬
slides.content:
# The Building Block of the Web An HTML **element** is everything from the opening tag to the closing tag: ```html

This is a paragraph.

``` - **Opening tag:** `

` - **Content:** `This is a paragraph.` - **Closing tag:** `

` Together they form a complete **element**. Some elements can also have **attributes** that live inside the opening tag.

slides.title: Tag vs Element – Is There a Difference? 🤔
slides.content:
# Tags are the Markers, Elements are the Whole Package - A **tag** is just the angle‑bracket syntax, like `

` or `

`. - An **element** includes the tag(s) plus the content. - Think of it like this: the tag is the container label; the element is the container with its contents inside. In casual chat people often say "tag" when they mean "element". Now you know the distinction!

quizData.question: What is the difference between an HTML tag and an element?

options.text: They are exactly the same thing
A tag includes the content, an element does not
An element is the opening tag + content + closing tag; a tag is just the marker

quizData.explanation:
An element encompasses the whole structure, while a tag refers to the individual markers like `

`.

slides.title: The Opening Tag in Detail 🏷️
slides.content: # Inside the Opening Tag An opening tag can hold **attributes**. ```html Click here ``` - `` – closes the tag. Attributes are **name="value"** pairs. We'll explore them deeply in the next lesson.

quizData.question: Attributes can only appear in the closing tag.
quizData.explanation: Attributes are placed inside the **opening** tag. Closing tags never have attributes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Close Your Tags

Browsers can be forgiving and guess where a tag should close, but relying on that leads to messy, unpredictable pages. Closing every tag makes your code clean and professional.
